issues.failure_explanation: On every convex polygonal domain the Poisson Dirichlet problem has H^2 regularity, i.e. $-\Delta: H^2(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)\to L^2(\Omega)$ is an isomorphism, so $\Delta^{-1}:L^2(\Om)\to H^2_0(\Om)$ is bounded; the failure of H^2 regularity occurs on non-convex domains (e.g. domains with reentrant corners). The clause 'even on convex domains' is therefore false, and it is also inconsistent with the paper's own standing use of convexity as the hypothesis that delivers H^2/H^3 regularity (prop:elliptic) and with the convergence results stated 'on convex polygonal domains'.

failure_location.quote: $\Delta^{-1}\colon L^2(\Om) \to H^2_0(\Om)$ which does not hold in general even on convex domains.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the sentence to '...which does not hold in general' (deleting 'even on convex domains'), or specify that the failure occurs on non-convex polygonal domains.
issues.overall_effect: The false claim is confined to an isolated remark expressing doubt about whether $\partial_t\psi\in L^2(I\times\Om)$; no theorem, lemma, or proof invokes it, and the regularity properties the paper actually relies on (convex-domain biharmonic H^3 regularity, prop:weak_stability) are stated correctly elsewhere.
issues.title: Remark falsely claims Poisson H^2 regularity fails even on convex domains
issues.why_classification: The error is an isolated false clause in a remark; the repair is a short rewording to the standard fact, and no formal result, guarantee, or downstream argument depends on the claim.

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiating the displayed pressure correction gives $\nabla(10^5(1.49\,x_1^{1.49})^{-1}) = -10^5\,x_1^{-2.49}\,e_1$, which is not the added field $10^5\,x_1^{-0.49}\,e_1 = \tilde\ff-\ff$. The two displayed formulas are therefore incompatible: the displayed $\tilde p$ is not a potential for the displayed perturbation. The actual potential of the perturbation $10^5\,x_1^{-0.49}e_1$ is $\frac{10^5}{0.51}x_1^{0.51}$.

failure_location.quote: and only the pressure changes to $\tilde p = p + 10^5 (1.49 \cdot x_1^{1.49})^{-1}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the two displays consistent by correcting one exponent: either use the perturbation $\tilde\ff = \ff + 10^5(x_1^{0.49},0)^T$ (keeping the displayed pressure) or use the pressure correction $\tilde p = p + \frac{10^5}{0.51}x_1^{0.51}$ (keeping the displayed perturbation).
issues.overall_effect: Only the numerical demonstration's explicit pressure formula is wrong. The qualitative conclusions of the experiment (a gradient perturbation leaves the velocity unchanged and changes only the pressure; the stream-function method is pressure robust) remain valid for either consistent choice, and no formal convergence result is affected.
issues.title: Displayed pressure correction is inconsistent with the displayed gradient-field perturbation
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-character exponent change in one of two mutually inconsistent displayed formulas, and every substantive claim of the demonstration and of the paper survives unchanged.
